dossier.public_summary: The dip appears and disappears a lot: sector depths are 8420, 3897 and 6842 ppm (a 71% change) and the four transits are inconsistent, as is common for detrending artifacts or systematics locked to the observing schedule. With a faint 13.39 Tmag M dwarf, this unstable depth and the near chance alignment of transits makes an eclipsing binary or planet unlikely compared to noise/variable depth.

reasons.why: Depth changes 70.82% between sectors (8420, 3897, 6842 ppm, err 1814, 584, 1040 ppm) with chi2 10.2 for 2 dof. sector_depths_by_source verdict is changes_within_a_source with p_constant 0.006095077679440219, not a calibration offset.
Individual transit depths scatter is significant with chi2 10.765288472284883 for 3 dof over 4 transits (mean 4921 ppm, share_of_top_3 0.803), not consistent with a single planet depth.

3 transits (refit.transits 3, but 4 seen) occur at expected near_gap positions with expected_share 0.2236, favouring that the signal is driven by a few events/notches rather than a true period 13.1 d signal.
Separate scorer rates the signal far below median planet (0.5), in the regime where only 1 in 10 planets score this low and false positives are common, supporting the variable-depth interpretation.

Centroid shows no sector with a clear difference image, so on-target cannot be established despite neighbours.plausible_within_1px 0 and closest_that_could at 30.7 arcsec (no centroid to rule out blend).
